Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

respect verb

keep to, not violate (a rule, a right, someone’s wishes)

also respect the rules, respect the law, respect someone’s wishes, respect others, be considerate

classical

Cic. Off. 2.40: lēgēs latrōnum esse dīcuntur, quibus pāreant, quās observent
Caes. BG 5.35 (Lewis & Short)

observō, observāre, observāvī, observātum

verb, first conjugation

keep, comply with, respect (a law, a rule, an agreement)

Lewis & Short: “to observe, respect, regard, attend to, heed, keep, comply with a law, precept, recommendation, etc.” For respect for a person see respect (esteem).

Other words

  • ratiōnem habēre (+ genitive) — have regard for, take into account (others, their interests)

    also used · classical · Cic. Off. 1.139: habenda ratiō nōn sua sōlum, sed etiam aliōrum

    See also consider (think about).

  • verēcundia, verēcundiae f. — respect for others’ feelings, consideration; modesty

    noun, first declension · also used · classical · Cic. Off. 1.99: jūstitiae partēs sunt nōn violāre hominēs, verēcundiae nōn offendere

    With a genitive, “respect for”: lēgum, for the laws (Liv. 10.13.8, Lewis & Short). The opposite of respecting a law or a person is violāre.

Examples

  • Quīn etiam lēgēs latrōnum esse dīcuntur, quibus pāreant, quās observent.

    Why, even robbers are said to have laws that they obey and respect.Cic. Off. 2.40

  • est autem quod differat in hominum ratiōne habendā inter jūstitiam et verēcundiam. Jūstitiae partēs sunt nōn violāre hominēs, verēcundiae nōn offendere

    But in the regard we pay to people, justice and respect differ: it is the part of justice not to wrong people, of respect not to offend themCic. Off. 1.99

  • ut in cēterīs habenda ratiō nōn sua sōlum, sed etiam aliōrum

    as in everything else, one must have regard not only for oneself but for others tooCic. Off. 1.139

See also respect, consider, obedient, rule.
